newsitem.title: UK: UK Government seen poised for interest rate rise.
newsitem.headline: UK Government seen poised for interest rate rise.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government appeared poised to raise interest rates on Tuesday after a meeting between new finance minister Gordon Brown and the Bank of England governor Eddie George was brought forward by one day, analysts said.
The UK Treasury said the meeting, originally scheduled for Wednesday had started at 0700 GMT and Brown was due to make a statement at 1000 GMT.
Analysts are widely expecting the meeting to result in a rise of at least 25 basis points in Britain's 6.0 percent interest rates.

They said Brown's decision to bring the meeting forward showed he was prepared to take the initiative on interest rates and would avoid giving the impression that he had been forced into a tightening of credit by the Bank of England.
Previous Conservative Chancellor Kenneth Clarke had resisted Bank of England calls to raise rates before last Thursday's election which the Labour party won with a landslide victory.
David Coleman, the chief economist at CIBC, said, "I think they're going to announce a 25 basis point increase in base rates."

Coleman said the early meeting showed Brown was willing to take tough decisions. "From a credibility perspective it's very encouraging. It will probably be the easiest rate increase he'll ever get to make," he said.
Ian Gunner, an economist at Chase Investment Bank, said "It looks like we're going to get a quarter-point rate rise."
He added, "The change in timing suggests Brown is keen to make a forceful move and take the initiative. This should be good for the markets and positive for sterling."
The Bank of England has been calling for an interest rate rise to take some upward pressure off the economy, especially in the area of wage costs.
But some industrialists are worried higher interest rates will push up an already strong pound sterling even further and increase the damage on the country's exports.
Adair Turner, head of the powerful Confederation of British Industry, said this week the government should dampen demand by tightening fiscal policy rather than raising interest rates.

Sterling ticked higher after news of the meeting, UK government bond prices also rose but the FTSE share index slowed down a little after opening at a new all time record on the back of a blistering rally on Monday night in the US.
